official.deadline_note: The official page publishes the window as 15 July - 1 September and the timeline is stated only for the 2026 round (review 5 September - 3 October 2026, award notifications November 2026). EASL has not yet published dates for the next round.
official.application_cycle: 2026 round - call for applications 15 July - 1 September 2026
official.status_note: The EASL Fellowships overview page states 'Applications are now closed'; the 2026 application window closed on 1 September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is not listed among the published budget categories. The budget template covers travel and accommodation costs (mobility fellowships only), salary / living expenses, laboratory supplies, equipment and research-related expenses, and other logistical costs deemed necessary for the successful execution of the fellowship, including childcare if applicable.
benefits: Up to EUR 25,000 per fellowship, depending on factors such as host institution location, travel costs, and research needs
Travel and accommodation costs (mobility fellowships only)
Laboratory supplies, equipment, and research-related expenses
Other logistical costs deemed necessary for the successful execution of the fellowship, including childcare if applicable
The grant budget should also cover attendance and participation at a future EASL Congress to present the project results
eligibility: Open to early- or mid-career professionals
Applicants must be affiliated with a recognised clinical / scientific institution or university in Europe
The host institute must be based in Europe
The research or project focus must be on liver disease
Must show strong motivation for pursuing a career in clinical or basic hepatology research (research fellowships only)
A letter from the host institute confirming the ability to host the applicant is required (mobility fellowships only)
In case of mobility fellowships, the selection process will favour applications that foster collaboration between institutions and contribute to knowledge exchange
requirements: Research/project proposal detailing the objectives, methodology, and expected impact of the research/project (max. 5 pages)
Motivation video (3-minute elevator pitch) outlining the applicant's research/project goals and motivation for applying
Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting academic, professional and personal achievements (max. 4 pages)
Recommendation letter from a supervisor or mentor supporting the application (max. 1 page)
Letter from host institute confirming the ability to host the applicant (max. 1 page) (mobility fellowships only)
Completed budget template and justification for the requested funding
An active EASL Membership is required to access the application portal
documents: Recommendation letter from a supervisor or mentor (max. 1 page)
Letter from host institute confirming the ability to host the applicant (max. 1 page) (mobility fellowships only)
Completed budget template and justification for the requested funding
selection_criteria: Scientific/Clinical merit - 35% - the quality, feasibility, and innovation of the proposed research/project
Applicant's motivation - 20% - motivation, enthusiasm, and rationale for applying, as demonstrated in the video submission
Applicant's potential - 15% - the candidate's background, research/clinical experience, and potential for future contributions to hepatology
Relevance to hepatology - 15% - the research/project's alignment with EASL's mission and its potential impact on liver disease research

Host institution & environment - 15% - for mobility fellowships the quality and suitability of the host institution in providing the necessary training and resources; for research fellowships the quality and suitability of the home institution in providing necessary resources and support
Each application is scored out of 100, with funding awarded based on the highest overall scores; final selection decisions also consider diversity, equity, and potential for long-term impact
coverage: Travel and accommodation costs (mobility fellowships only)
Laboratory supplies, equipment, and research-related expenses
Other logistical costs deemed necessary for the successful execution of the fellowship, including childcare if applicable
Attendance and participation at a future EASL Congress to present the project results
application_method: Applications need to be submitted via the EASL Memberzone
An active EASL Membership is required to access the application portal
official.application_route: Apply online through the EASL Memberzone portal, which requires an active EASL membership.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published. Applicants must be affiliated with a recognised clinical / scientific institution or university in Europe, and the host institute must be based in Europe.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applicants from all European countries are eligible, and preference may be given to those from Inclusiveness Target Countries (emerging/developing countries) for mobility fellowships, in line with the programme's goals.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research or project focus must be on liver disease.
official.research_requirement: A research/project proposal (max. 5 pages) detailing objectives, methodology and expected impact, plus a 3-minute motivation video and a completed budget template with justification.
official.description: EASL is committed to fostering excellence in hepatology research and education, and offers funding to young investigators, clinicians, nurses and allied health professionals to enhance their research experience and professional development. The Mobility / Research Fellowship Programme funds short-term, six-month fellowships that enhance professional development, promote collaboration and advance liver research across Europe, through two routes: Mobility Fellowships, which support temporary mobility of researchers from emerging/developing countries to established countries or vice versa, and Research Fellowships, which support focused research projects on liver disease carried out at the fellow's home institution.
official.program_type: Short-term research and mobility fellowship (6 months)

applicant_utility.summary: EASL funds up to EUR 25,000 for a six-month liver-disease project, with just 3 awards per round, and the money is budgeted as salary or living costs, travel and accommodation (mobility route only), lab consumables and equipment, other logistics including childcare, plus attendance at a future EASL Congress. Because the review is a 100-point grid where scientific/clinical merit alone carries 35% and the host-institution environment carries another 15%, the strongest applications are genuinely two-way partnerships: a sharply feasible hepatology question that a named lab has agreed to host. Only active EASL members can open the portal, so treat the membership payment as a precondition, not an afterthought - trainee and postdoc membership is EUR 50, regular is EUR 250, and membership runs for 12 months from the date of payment. The 2026 window ran 15 July to 1 September 2026 and has closed, so plan for the same mid-summer opening next year rather than waiting for the call to appear.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early- to mid-career hepatology researchers and clinicians at a European institution who want a six-month placement in another European lab (mobility) or funding for a focused project at their own (research).
application_readiness_checklist: Create or renew the EASL membership first and keep the payment confirmation date in mind - membership is valid for 12 months from payment, so a lapsed renewal blocks portal access on deadline day
Secure the host lab agreement in writing before drafting: mobility applicants need a signed host-institute letter confirming the ability to host, capped at 1 page
Build the budget in the four published cost lines (travel/accommodation, salary/living, lab supplies and equipment, other logistics including childcare) and reserve money for EASL Congress attendance
Record and cut the 3-minute motivation video well before the closing week - it carries 20% of the score and is the only criterion a panel judges on your behalf if motivation scores weakly elsewhere
Ask the supervisor or mentor for the 1-page recommendation letter early, since it must be attached to the same submission
Rehearse a one-sentence liver-disease relevance statement; alignment with EASL's mission and impact on liver disease research is 15% of the score
common_rejection_risks: Proposing work that is only tangentially about liver disease - relevance to hepatology is a scored 15% block and the programme exists expressly to advance liver research
A weak or absent host-institution fit: the environment criterion is 15% and the panel judges whether the host can actually supply the training and resources the proposal assumes
Requesting costs outside the published budget categories, or asking for the full EUR 25,000 without a defensible line-by-line justification - the award is capped, not guaranteed

A route mismatch: research-fellowship motivation claims are only scored for that route, and mobility-only documents such as the host letter will be missing or misapplied if the wrong fellowship type is chosen
Over-length submissions: 5 pages for the proposal, 4 for the CV, 1 for the recommendation and 1 for the host letter are hard ceilings, not targets
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything not in the four budget lines: tuition or course fees are not covered, institutional overheads and bench fees outside the negotiated budget are not covered, visa and insurance costs are not itemised, and the grant only funds attendance at a future EASL Congress rather than other conferences. With only three awards per round, most applicants receive nothing regardless of quality.
document_audit: The budget template is described as 'download budget template' on the public page but the link is not live there - locate the current template through the Memberzone or the EASL office (easloffice@easloffice.eu) before the window closes, because a submission with an ad-hoc budget sheet instead of the template risks being discounted
The motivation video is an elevator pitch, not a research summary; a 3-minute file is easy to overrun, so time the final cut rather than assuming the recorder kept it to length
The 1-page host letter and the 1-page recommendation letter are separate documents - a single combined letter does not satisfy either requirement
The CV cap of 4 pages is strict; tailor it to hepatology research experience rather than pasting a complete publication list
alerts: Only 3 awards are made per round, so treat this as a competitive small-grant prize rather than a broadly available funding line
The award is 'up to EUR 25,000' and varies with host location, travel costs and research needs - do not plan the budget against the maximum
The window is short and seasonal (15 July - 1 September), roughly six weeks, which is tight for securing a host letter and editing a video
Mobility applications are scored with a preference for moves that create institutional collaboration and knowledge exchange, and preference may be given to Inclusiveness Target Countries
EASL membership is a hard gate, and the membership fee is paid by the applicant and is non-refundable
Award notifications land roughly two to three months after the deadline (November 2026 for the last round), so have a fallback funding plan for the start of the year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Log into the EASL Memberzone while the window is open, complete the online fellowship form, and upload the proposal, motivation video, CV, recommendation letter, host letter (mobility only) and budget template as attachments before the 1 September cut-off.
